Path 2, MCP managementGOALS §3.5

ToolHive

MCP servers as isolated, Kubernetes-native workloads.

WHAT IT IS

Stacklok's Apache-2.0 platform runs each MCP server in its own container. Its operator bundles a runtime, registry and gateway, and creates a scoped ServiceAccount and RBAC for every MCP server.

WHAT SETS IT APART

Isolation and per-server identity by default, closer to how we run any other service. More operational weight for teams without cluster expertise.

WHERE WE STAND

In the bake-off against Obot.

Stacklok documentation; "Cedar Analysis for MCP Servers", KubeCon NA 2026

DECIDE

ToolHive: MCP servers as isolated, Kubernetes-native workloads. Where we stand: In the bake-off against Obot. If the enforcement point is per-server identity, ToolHive fits; if it's a central catalog and gateway, Obot fits.
